title: HarvestAI edge deploy — TF constraints and rollout notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working draft for the HarvestAI private deployment (edge/VPC) focused on small regional collocated sites across three rural datacenters. Goal: support low-latency inference for on-prem user terminals and allow periodic sync to central region when bandwidth permits. Document covers high-level sizing assumptions, Terraform module notes, upgrade/rollback process, and a checklist for the first pilot site.

Key customer constraints and context:
- Customer: HarvestAI (agritech SaaS) — strict data residency per country; cannot send raw field sensor payloads off-site without explicit consent.
- Sites: 6 pilot sites, each in small colocation facility with 1U racks available.
- Connectivity: intermittent 10–50 Mbps uplinks; windows of higher bandwidth at night. Packet loss up to 1–3% during storms.
- Power: single utility feed in 4/6 sites; UPS available but runtime limited (~30 minutes).
- Maintenance window: weekly 02:00–06:00 local time.
- Security: customer-managed KMS/HSM; requires integration for model keys and audit logs to be shipped to their SIEM.

SLA targets (negotiated, pilot):
- P99 response latency for typical chat/generation use-case <= 450 ms local (token streaming permitted).
- Uptime target: 99.5% per site (pilot), with automated fallbacks to central region when connectivity is available.
- RTO target for full site replacement: 4 hours.

Sizing assumptions (per site):
- Workload: mixed interactive chat + batch embedding extraction. Typical concurrency: 8 parallel sessions during peak; rare peaks to 20.
- Avg request: 120 tokens input, 256 tokens output, average generation length 150 tokens.
- Throughput target: ~1500 tokens/sec sustained across all sessions.
- Latency target: cold-start (no KV cache) < 600ms; warm < 250ms.

Hardware recommendation (pilot profile):
- 1x rack node (1U preferred): NVIDIA T4 or A10 GPU (if available) with 64–128 GB system RAM. T4 if cost/thermal constrained; A10 for better perf/cost for mixed workloads.
- CPU: 16 vCPU equivalent (EPYC-class) to handle I/O and batching.
- Local storage: 2 TB NVMe (model cache + swap + logs). Encrypted at rest by customer KMS.
- Optional: small dedicated NVRAM for journaling if using local DB for sync.
- Network: 2x 1Gb uplink with bonding. Local VLAN for inference traffic.

Rationale: single-GPU node per site keeps power and space requirements low; model caching + prefix KV will be used to keep latency low. If site requires higher concurrency, run two nodes and let smart routing split traffic (see rollout).

Terraform module notes (intent / variables / pitfalls):
- Modules we will reuse/extend: ri_vpc_edge, ri_node_edge, ri_kms_connector, ri_prometheus_exporter_edge, ri_tf_remote_state

- ri_vpc_edge (purpose): create local management VPC and subnets, security groups limiting inbound to customer-managed jump host and Redwood health checks.
  - input vars (expected): site_id, cidr_block, allowed_admin_cidrs, datacenter_rack_id, mgmt_subnet_tags
  - outputs (useful): vpc_id, management_subnet_id, bastion_sg_id
  - NOTES: customer requires explicit route table tagging for audit; add variable enforce_route_tags = true

- ri_node_edge (purpose): provision node(s) in coloc, supports both cloud providers and baremetal via DHCP + provisioning script.
  - input vars: node_count, gpu_type (T4|A10|A30), node_size, storage_nvme_gb, ssh_keys, forward_logs_to
  - pitfalls: baremetal provisioning requires longer timeouts in the provider; ensure ttl and retries increased; we need a separate var: provisioning_retry_count = 10

- ri_kms_connector (purpose): configure customer KMS/HSM endpoints and set up least-privilege service account.
  - input vars: kms_endpoint, key_aliases (list), roles_allowed, log_forwarder_endpoint
  - NOTES: for customers using HSM, we must provide a stubbed local token during bootstrap and rotate once HSM is reachable. Add var allow_kms_stub = true (default false)

- ri_prometheus_exporter_edge
  - makes a node-exporter + prometheus pushgateway config for intermittent connectivity. Use push model to central Prometheus when uplink healthy.
  - var: push_interval_seconds = 300 (tunable); fallback_store_local_days = 3

Remote state considerations:
- Use local S3-compatible object store (minio) in central region for state with signed temporary credentials for on-site apply. For fully air-gapped sites we will store state on encrypted USB passepartout and keep a signed manifest in central remote-state. Add tag remote_state_mode = "hybrid"

Upgrade and rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 — Prep (2 weeks)
- Run a compatibility test at Redwood staging with same TF modules against a simulated disconnected network (throttle to 10 Mbps, 2% loss).
- Confirm model artifact size and push/pull mechanics.
- Prepare customer KMS onboarding — exchange certs, validate HSM endpoints.

Phase 1 — Pilot deploy (single site) (1 week)
- Apply ri_vpc_edge + ri_node_edge with node_count=1.
- Deploy inference runtime with container image pinned to tag v0.9.0-rc1.
- Run smoke tests: local generation, embeddings, KV-warm etc.
- Observe telemetry for 72 hours.

Phase 2 — Canary upgrade (per-site) (2 days per site)
- Use canary traffic (10%) and monitor latency/cost/quality.
- If regressions, auto-fallback policy to central hosted API (graceful degrade).

Phase 3 — Fleet rollout (4–6 weeks)
- Incremental add of sites in batches of 2.
- Nightly synchronization windows for model updates.

Rollback plan:
- If upgrade causes >5% increase in P99 latency or >2% error rate for 15 minutes, trigger automatic rollback to previous container image and restore previous TF-managed route settings.
- In TF terms: maintain immutable tags for node groups; use terraform taint/untain pattern with prebuilt images so revert is a single terraform apply.

Operational patterns for intermittent connectivity:
- Local inference must be fully functional offline for at least 48 hours. Sync daemon will push logs and metrics when link is healthy.
- Model updates are delivered as delta artifacts to minimize transfer size. Use rsync + zstd compression for model shards.
- Prometheus push model with local retention to avoid datapoint loss.

Monitoring / Observability:
- Metrics: request_latency_ms, tokens_generated, model_cache_hit_ratio, gpu_utilization, disk_io, network_drop_rate
- Alerts: p99_latency > 600ms (critical), model_cache_hit_ratio < 45% (warning), disk_free < 10% (warning)
- Logs: send structured audit logs to customer SIEM via secure forwarder; store only metadata off-site; raw payloads remain local unless consented.

Security and compliance notes:
- Default: encrypt models at rest using customer KMS; keys must never be stored plaintext on disk.
- All control-plane operations via a customer-managed bastion with MFA.
- Provide a minimal RBAC profile for local ops: ops_readonly, ops_infer, ops_admin (bastion-only).

Open questions / action items (todo):
- Q1: Confirm GPU family preference and available vendor support at each colocation (T4 vs A10). (Action: Solution Eng to collect vendor rack inventory)
- Q2: Confirm whether customer will accept delta model updates or requires full image/sha checks per update. (Action: CS to confirm)
- Q3: Decide remote_state_mode final: hybrid vs fully-central (Action: Infra to propose DR plan)
- Q4: Get customer agreement on failover policy to central hosted API for PII data flows (Action: Legal + CS)

Pilot site checklist (pre-deploy):
- [ ] Exchange KMS certs and test HSM access
- [ ] Provide SSH keys and jump host cidr list
- [ ] Confirm rack power test (must sustain >400W for node)
- [ ] Confirm network baseline (run 24h throughput test)
- [ ] Approve remote_state_mode and TF timeouts
- [ ] Smoke-test fallback to central API

Estimated ballpark costs (per site, monthly amortized pilot):
- HW amortization: $950–1,800/month (depends on GPU)
- Bandwidth: $50–200/month
- Support / maintenance (Redwood placeholder): $1,500/month per site during pilot

Notes and references:
- Prototype TF snippets used in staging: see linked GitHub branch (edge-templates).
- Compatibility tests still outstanding for model quantization profile on T4 (TODO: Priya to run quant test by 2025-03-07).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep ri_kms_connector conservative; customer HSM onboarding always takes longer than expected.
- For low-power sites, consider throttling batch size to prioritize latency over throughput.
- If we see persistent >2% packet loss, add local LB + FEC layer to reduce tail latency.

End of draft.
